The time seperation function has the following properties:
• τ(y, y′) = 0 if y′ and y are not cuassally related,
• τ(y, y′) > 0 if y ≪y′.

If F is an intrinsic metric space, then −I ×f F is a Lorentzian pre-length
space in the sense of [KS18].
Here we collect some properties of −I ×f F. We always assume that F is
intrinsic.
• −I ×f F has the push-up property: if (s, x) ≪(t, y) if and only if
there exists a future directed causal curve from (s, x) to (t, y) with
